Subject: Order Form question — exchange rate treatment for true-ups

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prepare the counter-signature, procurement raised a quick question on the pricing exhibit around currency treatment: we invoice in USD, but our reporting and budgeting run in EUR. The Order Form references a quarterly true-up and legacy credits for overage/underage, but it's silent on which FX rate to use and whether the cap/floor thresholds are applied pre- or post-conversion.

Specifically:
- For the quarterly true-up, do you apply the bank-of-record spot rate on the invoice date (USD -> EUR) or a monthly average?
- If a legacy credit is due (e.g., when a previous commit was overestimated), is that credit calculated in USD and then converted for our books, or is it calculated in EUR based on a specified rate in the contract?

We have an internal policy to avoid retroactive FX adjustments that change revenue recognition. If you have standard contract language that clarifies both the rate source and rounding/proration rules, that would help speed this along.

I attached the draft Order Form with our non-substantive comments (ACME_OrderForm_v3.pdf). If you prefer to propose redline text for the pricing exhibit, that works too — send it over and we'll review with finance.

Appreciate your help,

Liam O'Neill
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Cloud

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear note and the attachment. Quick answers up front: we bill and track commitments in USD as stated on the Order Form, but we can add explicit language that (1) defines the FX rate source for conversions, (2) clarifies whether caps/floors are evaluated pre- or post-conversion, and (3) documents rounding/proration rules for credits so both parties have consistent revenue recognition.

I'll loop in Marissa (AE) and Karthik (legal) to propose contract wording. In most past deals we: 
- Calculate all thresholds (caps/floors and commit bands) in the contract currency (USD).
- Convert any customer-reported local-currency numbers to USD for true-up calculations using the FX source and look-back window specified in an exhibit.
- Use the spot rate published by the Federal Reserve (or another mutually agreed source) on the invoice date for single-event adjustments, or a monthly average for multi-month proration.

If ACME prefers EUR-native calculations for invoicing/true-up, we can make that an exception and bind the pricing exhibit to EUR with a fixed FX policy for the term.

Marissa/Karthik — can you propose terse redline language (2–3 sentences) we can insert into Exhibit B (Pricing & True-up) and highlight any downstream implications to billing/collections/finance?

Best,

Quick commercial note from my side: Acme is asking for EUR-native true-ups only for reporting convenience, but we should avoid shifting our billing currency unless Acme wants the pricing bands and caps converted and sealed to EUR for the term — that has downstream effects on invoicing automation and collections (workload for Finance).

If ACME wants EUR as the contract currency we can do it, but it typically: 
- Requires us to lock an FX policy for the term (to avoid accounting churn), and
- Pushes a small implementation effort for invoicing templates.

Liam / ACME team — attached is a concise redline for Exhibit B (redline_pricing_exhibit_markup.docx). Key points in plain language below so it's easier to review in email: 

1) Contract currency and thresholds: All commit bands, caps and floors shall be denominated in United States Dollars (USD) unless the parties execute a written amendment electing EUR as the contract currency. Thresholds are evaluated against the USD-denominated amounts.

2) Conversion for customer reports/credits: Where Customer reports usage in a non-USD currency, Redwood will convert reported amounts to USD for true-up calculation using the ECB monthly average rate for the month in which the usage occurred, published on the first business day following the month-end.

3) Single-event adjustments and invoice-date conversions: For one-time adjustments (including legacy credits), the parties will apply the Federal Reserve noon spot rate on the invoice date (or another mutually agreed public rate) to convert to Customer's local currency for Customer accounting purposes.

4) Rounding and proration: All converted amounts will be rounded to two decimal places in the currency presented on the invoice. Proration for partial-period credits will be based on full days of service during the billing period.

5) No retroactive FX re-calculation: Except as required by law, neither party will seek to retroactively re-calculate previously settled invoices for FX variance after 180 days from the invoice date.

If ACME is okay with this approach we can (a) insert the attached markup into Exhibit B and (b) update the billing/invoicing ticket for Finance to ensure templates align with the selected FX sources. Marissa — ask Finance to estimate the minor template work if Liam confirms.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Thanks Karthik — the redline looks sensible and the 180-day finality clause is acceptable to Acme's finance team. Two small asks before we countersign: 

1) Can we add an explicit example sentence showing an illustrative calculation for a legacy credit (so our auditors can see the math)? Something like: "Example: A €100,000 reported overage for May would be converted to USD using the ECB monthly average for May (EUR->USD = 1.10), resulting in a $110,000 credit before rounding/proration."

2) Please confirm that applying the ECB monthly average (for reports) and the Fed spot (for invoice-date items) will not create overlapping adjustments that lead to double crediting. We want to be sure the two rules are mutually exclusive by outcome (reports -> converted via monthly average for true-up; one-off invoice corrections -> Fed spot on invoice date).

If you add the example sentence and a clarifying line about exclusivity, we're good to countersign. Can you also send a DocuSign link once the updated exhibit is in?

Appreciate the swift turn,

Liam
